decisions.reason: October 8 publication is within the frozen September 16–October 15 window. Accept as an operational evaluation tutorial useful for students designing task-specific agent tests, not evidence of model superiority. The saved passage under “The fix” recommends fresh chats with the same files and tools and asks humans to approve the task and criteria; this supplies a concrete procedure, rather than a demonstrated research advance. The author's claim that ChatGPT was better concerns one scoped demonstration; linked outputs are not included in the supplied evidence, and repeated trials, held-out tasks and comparable budgets are not established. “Do this now” recommends an AI judge, including ChatGPT judging a comparison involving its own output: require human review as a safeguard, without asserting demonstrated bias. Footnote 6 acknowledges differing judge scores of 92 and 93; neither establishes superiority. “Dig deeper” promotes paid access to Fun Bench, creating a subscription interest. Evidence: [saved text, “The fix,” “Do this now,” “Dig deeper,” and footnote 6](/Users/ww/Desktop/26f/software/ps04/data/assets/075b80e31faba3a92a3d7712/6d392f0b897d89aba5f23830f5b954824cd8a50f3e5b222e12b93c42db9bf552/text.txt).

September 30 publication is within the frozen window. Accept this researcher-authored account for its concrete research-loop design and reward-misalignment example. In “A better PLM recipe,” Li and Lu report contact precision rising from 28.2% to 36.6% at a matched 48.4B-token budget, explicitly with a human deciding which recipes to scale. Attribute this result to the authors; it is not a fully autonomous discovery or independently replicated finding. “Failure mode” reports that validation-loss improvements did not deliver the strongest contact precision, directly informing student choices of reward and scientific evaluation. “What survived the human gate” describes two seeds per candidate and four of seven changes surviving scaled ablation. These safeguards are useful, but the supplied blog lacks the underlying ablation tables, execution logs and hardware details needed to audit performance or estimate student reproduction costs; contact precision remains a proxy. The authors promote their own research environment, and their referenced paper belongs to the same evidence lineage, not independent corroboration. Evidence: [saved text, the three named sections and “Authors and links”](/Users/ww/Desktop/26f/software/ps04/data/assets/084a91218ed6d51df5ab9f17/2b0d8382c674620fd174f5c60697d5bdf4728371aa386ebba1986c60e1eef65b/text.txt).

September 30 publication is within the frozen window. Accept for methodological discussion and evidence scrutiny; withhold faster-execution, lower-cost and best-result conclusions pending numeric clarification. Sections 3.2–3.4 describe the useful contribution: preserving untried ideas alongside compatible executable states and feeding evaluator results back into search. Section 4 specifies an M4 Pro with 24 GB memory, one-hour or twelve-hour horizons, named baselines and differing task objectives; these make the authors' study inspectable without proving general superiority. Explicit unresolved inconsistency: Table 4 reports AutoMIP's sole 6–12-hour MINLPLib success at 41,089 seconds, while Appendix H records its sole success in that interval, acopf_caseactivsg70k_qcqp, at 24,199 seconds. Likewise Table 3 gives NoPool's sole 6–12-hour success as 42,334 seconds, versus 35,403 for sct1 in Appendix F. Do not average these discrepancies away. The supplied extraction also leaves several protocol appendix sections empty, and outcome tables lack objective values needed to verify best-solution claims. This is the developers' preprint evaluation, with no independent replication or conflict disclosure supplied. Evidence: [saved text, §§3–4, Tables 3–4, Appendices A, F and H](/Users/ww/Desktop/26f/software/ps04/data/assets/090f19610270f1b804a5bb8a/bc44cd416a3cec196c5ff3ae89d1d7f5f529cfcb851b97b519470fc6baccac09/text.txt).

October 7 publication is within the frozen window. Accept for the concrete separation of agent proposals from trusted kernel construction, frozen validation selection and held-out testing. Appendix A.6 reports hidden-test failures in 12/35, 18/31 and 8/37 numerically screened programs; these are author-reported stress-test cohorts, not universal agent failure rates. Proposition 1 and Appendix A.1 condition kernel validity on finite outputs and domain-wide purity: sampled conformance tests do not prove those assumptions. Appendix B.5 supplies matched search ablations but changes several mechanisms together in the independent-proposal arm. Examine counterevidence explicitly: Appendix B.7 finds frozen DWF wins only 4/16 real-data comparisons, and Appendix D.3 finds forecasting gains concentrated in reversed windows while CAKE performs better on the ten-year forward diagnostic. Appendix C.8 identifies the additive refinement as human-defined; its improvement must not be attributed solely to autonomous discovery. Students can adapt the verification and split-and-freeze design, but Appendix D.1's token and timing reports lack enough hardware and pricing detail for a portable cost claim. This remains an author-led preprint study; no independent replication or author conflict disclosure is supplied. Evidence: [saved text, Proposition 1 and Appendices A.1, A.6, B.5, B.7, C.8 and D.1–D.3](/Users/ww/Desktop/26f/software/ps04/data/assets/0ff8643be07c7b70497b5caf/b5c10a5a1f3bc0adb95fe7a8ee96127189a24131d2304c6d0f00b108ccee3a5f/text.txt).
